The Q&A following the film will be livestreamed from the Worklight Pictures Warehouse Theater at the Contemporary Arts Center.

Join us after as we second line to Gallier Hall!

events.title: Opening Night Party
events.blurb:
Following the New Orleans Film Festival’s opening‑night premiere of Ben Chace’s Victory, guests will step into the beautiful Gallier Hall for a late‑night party that celebrates the start of the New Orleans Film Festival. Set in the historic former New Orleans City Hall, the evening features local food, cocktails and live music by Cha Wa that mirror the heart and excitement of the city. This is an exclusive chance to celebrate opening night with artists, filmmakers and fans.

Sponsored by:

events.title: A Hands-On Introduction to 35mm Filmmaking, presented by Shawscope - Part I
events.blurb:
In Part I of this workshop, you’ll get a crash course in shooting celluloid film, and then in Part II (pre-registration required) you'll get your hands on 35mm movie cameras used on films like “Queen and Slim”, “City of God”, “A Clockwork Orange”, and “For The Grind” (screening at NOFF!). Each workshop participant will get a chance to shoot a shot on 35mm, and receive a downloadable digital file of the workshop footage for their own use.

Sponsored by:

events.title: Virtual Production in Practice: Making the Impossible Shot Possible
events.blurb:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.

Producer Erik Weaver (USC ETC) and director C. Craig Patterson (Fathead, ChikaBOOM!) trade notes on building worlds inside LED volume stages. They'll unpack how virtual production lets filmmakers build impossible worlds and turn creative constraints into visionary opportunities.

events.title: Lunch & Learn: Mindfulness for Filmmakers
events.blurb:
Film sets demand long hours, early call times, constant problem-solving, standing on your feet, unpredictable meals, and the ability to stay focused and creative under pressure.

Drawing from his book Sadhana: A Modern Spiritual Routine for a Healthier, Happier Life, Mark Berger will share practical mindfulness, movement, breath, and spiritual practices that actors, directors, producers, and production crews can use before call time, between setups, during meal breaks, and after wrap. We’ll explore simple ways to manage stress and anxiety, maintain energy, support physical health, and avoid letting the demands of production take over your well-being.

Designed specifically for the realities of working in the film industry, this lunch-and-learn offers tools that can be practiced in five minutes or woven into your entire day on set.

Sponsored by:

events.title: NOFF37 Ribbon Cutting
events.blurb:
FREE AND OPEN TO THE PUBLIC

The Ribbon Cutting Ceremony marks the official opening of the Festival Hub at the Contemporary Arts Center and the start of the 37th New Orleans Film Festival presented by Andscape. Filmmakers, civic and business leaders, area chambers of commerce, press, and festival guests gather as NOFS leadership welcomes the city into the Hub and honors the year's Cultural Ambassadors. The ceremony flows directly into South Pitch Narrative, so the Hub is full and buzzing from the first moment.

events.title: South Pitch Narrative Competition
events.blurb:
Admission is free and open to the public.

South Pitch is a high-energy showcase of the distinctive stories and filmmaking talent emerging from the American South.

Now in its 16th season, South Pitch is one of the New Orleans Film Festival’s signature industry programs, connecting Southern filmmakers with the funding, mentorship, and industry access to help move ambitious projects forward. Each year, five documentary and five narrative teams take the stage for five minutes to pitch their works-in-progress before a panel of industry leaders, who provide feedback and award additional funding to selected projects.

-----

In preparation for the pitch, every participating team receives one-on-one pitch training, a minimum $1,500 grant, travel support, and All-Access passes to the New Orleans Film Festival. The industry panel selects a winner and runner-up in both the documentary and narrative categories for additional funding, while audience members get a voice of their own, awarding a $500 Audience Award in each category.

Pitchers include:

Gerard Clarke and Rashielle Clarke (Acworth, Georgia) - Landfall: An immigrant girl must survive until dawn as Hurricane Andrew claws her family’s home open.

Nana Kumi (Natchez, Mississippi) - Blood for Soil: A woman awakens in a remote town with no recollection of how she arrived. She races to escape before its obscured past consumes her.

Christian Meola (Austin, Texas) - Other Days: Four college guy friends shatter their group dynamic when they realize a deeper need to be closer to each other across three stories.

Nolam Plaas (New Orleans, Louisiana) and Louis Anania (New York) - pecan: Junie and his father, Kenny, attempt to live up to expectations of being men.

Ivan Rome (Columbus, Georgia) - Hallelujah Night: A pastor's kid and his two best friends sneak out for their first Halloween party.

Sponsored by:

events.title: Stewards of History: Local Archive Collections & Their Hidden Treasures
events.blurb:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.

Join local organizations for a conversation exploring the vital work of collecting, preserving, and protecting the documents that tell our region's story. Come learn what's in the archives, how to access them, and how this work anchors a community's identity.

events.title: Calling Back Our Disappearing Acts: Working with Personal Archives
events.blurb:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.

This panel takes a closer look at films that farm the personal past in order to gain new perspectives on inherited (her)stories and reclaim them as our own. Together we will contemplate personal, familial archives as living, creative partners in conversation with our filmmaking practices.

events.title: Zenón and the Rebel Boats
events.blurb: A biographical documentary about the life of fisherman, Carlos "Taso" Zenón who led the fishermen movement in Vieques to halt US Navy war games in the Caribbean Sea.

events.title: Three Times (Tres Tiempos)
events.blurb: In a house between the mountains, facing a mirrored lake, Emma and her teenage granddaughter Alicia live together. Emma instills her passion for dance and raises Alicia as a mother, but Alicia falls prey to her controlling upbringing. The unexpected arrival of Barbara, Alicia’s mother and Emma’s daughter, accompanied by her caregiver, disrupts the routine of their small world.

events.title: Animated Shorts: Tactile Visions
events.blurb: This year’s block showcases a variety of mediums, broadening our conception of the animated film. From embroidered rituals, to journeys in clay, to the blobbiest and most colorful of brushstroke encounters, these beauties almost beckon you to reach out and touch.

events.title: The Haunting of Pennhurst
events.blurb: For over 70 years, Pennhurst State School & Hospital was called a place of care. What happened inside killed over half its population. After closing in 1987, it left behind unmarked graves and an unresolved history. Today, on those same grounds, disabled performers prepare to scare visitors at the Pennhurst Asylum haunted attraction.

events.title: Cinema Reset: Cyanotype Animation!
events.blurb:
This hands-on workshop combines the beautiful 19th century cyanotype photographic process with stop-motion animation. Using paper pre-coated with emulsion, we’ll arrange stencils, objects, and 16mm negatives, expose contact prints to sunlight, and process the images with water. They’ll then be scanned and incorporated into a collaborative animation which will be projected at the Independent Filmmaker Party on Monday night. You keep your cyanotype prints!

All ages welcome (though children must be supervised by an adult), no experience necessary. Bring small items to create your own animated silhouettes!

Workshop Facilitated by Rachel Lynn Weaver and Tacie Jones

Cinema Reset is the NOFF expanded media showcase. Founded in 2011, the showcases groundbreaking projects at the intersections film, art, technology, and performance. We also offer workshops to share unique creative resources with the New Orleans community. Cinema Reset is curated by Rachel Lin Weaver.

But the illusion shatters when a stranger on the street, Mechi, recognizes the dog… as HER boyfriend Danny’s dog. Fueled by betrayal and questionable judgment, the two launch a mission to get even.

events.title: I Play Rocky

events.title: Cinema Reset: Time According to Sweet Wreath
events.blurb:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.

A mythopoetic tale about media, memory, and the constellation of artists & freethinkers in central Alabama known as Sweet Wreath. This expanded cinema performance by Jasper Lee weaves live scoring & spoken word with montages of super8 footage, photographs, drawings, videos, and music from the Sweet Wreath archives.

Sweet Wreath is a project based in Alabama since 2016 which presents performances and publishes music, maps and books by artists working in the American underground & beyond. Notable releases include Johnny Coley's Mister Sweet Whisper, Silica Gel's Wooden Shoe, & Sun Ra's Magic City: A Cosmo-Mythic Map of Birmingham, among others. More info at www.sweetwreath.com.

Jasper Lee's work with sound & media includes performing in groups (with Johnny Coley, Vernal Scuzz, Silica Gel), making experimental films, and creating multimedia installations. Lee's work with the moving image includes art films and music videos which have screened at festivals internationally. His work with sound includes making instruments, radio art broadcasts, film scores and an array of recorded releases.

Cinema Reset is the NOFF expanded media showcase. Founded in 2011, the showcases groundbreaking projects at the intersections film, art, technology, and performance. We also offer workshops to share unique creative resources with the New Orleans community.

Cinema Reset is curated by Rachel Lin Weaver.

events.title: Louisiana Shorts: Forgotten Histories
events.blurb:
What can a place tell you about the people who came before? These two films travel through Louisiana’s schools, coastlines, and family histories to uncover stories of Black education and Filipino settlement that deserve to be remembered.

Shorts Block Sponsored by:

events.title: Narrative Shorts: Silver Linings
events.blurb:
This screening is offered as PAY WHAT YOU WILL. Everyone is welcome. No one is turned away. Whether you’re able to give a little, a lot, or nothing at all, we’re glad you’re here.

NOFF Passholders may still use their pass to scan in. NOFS Members may pay any amount in lieu of their traditional discount.

Limit of 2 tickets per person.

Caustic, paradoxical: the comedy in tragedy, the sweet with the spicy. These films conjure up a singular yet delicious combination of pathos and humor. Don’t let your family, your job, or your tech get you down… When things are at their dimmest, you can always find the light.

events.title: Mexicanamerican
events.blurb: Using present-day interviews and the VHS home movies his family once sent across the border, a filmmaker explores how and why his parents migrated to the US from Mexico, revealing a personal mosaic of one family's struggle to reconcile two cultures between two generations.

events.title: Lighting the Fuse: Films as Catalysts
events.blurb:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.

Films have the power to provoke and inspire. This panel explores how filmmakers are using cinema as an agent of change, and what it takes to make work that doesn't just reflect the world, but reshapes it.

events.title: Windows of Time
events.blurb: Filmmaker Hubert Taylor spent forty years capturing hundreds of hours of footage celebrating Black life in South Georgia, weaving an extraordinary archive into an intimate portrait of his father, the legendary gospel singer Brother Theotis Taylor.

events.title: Louisiana Shorts: Chicory
events.blurb: Deeply rooted in time and place, these films traverse tragic histories and ghostly ancestries, while others explore modern realities; hurricanes and electricity shut-offs. Cooking with complexly regional flavours, they each contribute something distinct to our cinematic landscape.

events.title: Singing the Shapes: Songs of the Enduring Sacred Harp
events.blurb: One of America's oldest living musical traditions, Sacred Harp singers form a curious subculture where participation gives rise to unexpected harmony across generations, beliefs, and ways of life.

events.title: Club Kid
events.blurb: The life of washed-up underground party promoter Peter takes an unexpected turn when he is forced to care for Arlo, a 10-year old son he never knew he had.

events.title: Michael Murphy Retrospective
events.blurb:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.

Join us for a look at the 35+ year careers of Emmy winners Michael Murphy & Cilista Eberle. Michael Murphy Productions is known for creating documentaries that spotlight New Orleans culture & music. Their films have been distributed Sony Pictures, Universal Music Group, and PBS. Their most recent film - The Dew Drop Inn: Resistance & Resilience - will have its world premiere at this years New Orleans Film Festival.

events.title: Isle Child + Sole (얼)
events.blurb: Feature film 'Isle Child' preceded by short film "Sole."

Feature film "Caity" preceded by short film "Blue."

events.title: Narrative Shorts: Queer Imaginaries
events.blurb: Queer politics and art allow us to scrutinize and restructure the limits of our shared realities. These shorts draw on their characters’ fantasies, hopes, and anxieties about the future (and the now), using the camera lens to transform dreams into tangible cinematic worlds.

events.title: The Welcome Table
events.blurb: People from all over the world displaced by climate change and extreme weather are invited to a single table on the levee in New Orleans to meet, talk to each other, and heal.

events.title: Singing the Shapes: Workshop & Group Sing
events.blurb:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.

Join us at the conference stage after the World Premiere of SINGING THE SHAPES for a shape singing workshop and group sing.

Shape-note singing is one of America’s oldest forms of music. The notation system—shape notes—is unique, and so is the four-part “dispersed harmony” that gives the music its distinctive force, often defying the expectations of modern choral sound.

No experience necessary.

events.title: Experimental Shorts: Wakeful Nature
events.blurb: When words fail us, these films explore the secrets of modern society alongside the mysteries of the natural world, and where they converge. From outer space to deep within the body, this program shows us what it means to be human (or not) with voices from around the globe.

events.title: Dew Drop Inn: Resistance and Resilience
events.blurb: Opening in 1939, The “Drop” helped launch the careers of iconic national and New Orleans artists. It was a critical stop on the Chitlin circuit; providing a safe haven for the Black community during segregation. This is a story of one man and his hotel and music venue that became symbols of resistance and resilience during the struggle for civil rights.

events.title: She Keeps Me Young
events.blurb:
This screening is offered as PAY WHAT YOU WILL. Everyone is welcome. No one is turned away. Whether you’re able to give a little, a lot, or nothing at all, we’re glad you’re here.

NOFF Passholders may still use their pass to scan in. NOFS Members may pay any amount in lieu of their traditional discount.

Limit of 2 tickets per person.

events.title: Test
events.blurb: An amateur bodybuilder in rural Ohio must confront a dysfunctional family, substance abuse, and his own emerging sexuality on his quest to become a champion.

events.title: A City in the Forest
events.blurb: In Atlanta, a decentralized resistance movement rallies to defend an urban forest from the construction of Cop City, the United States’ largest police training facility.

events.title: Paramount Presents: From Screen to Stage at The Dew Drop Inn
events.blurb:
FREE FOR NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!!

Join us at the historic Dew Drop Inn on Sunday night of the festival. Start the evening poolside for a laid-back cocktail hour, then settle in for live performances as the night unfolds — featuring a set from legend Bobby Rush. It's old-school cool at its finest, in a room steeped in New Orleans music history.

Sponsored by Paramount.

events.title: Write It Bad
events.blurb:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.

What if, instead of trying to write the right scene, you tried to write the absolute worst one? Join us for our first live screenwriting game!

Pull a prompt, give it a twist, and we'll set the clock to 10 minutes while you write a glorious mess. Chip away at writer's block by adding a wildly inappropriate character, making the stakes absurd, or completely derailing the scene. Then, with the help of some actors, we’ll bring a few of these “bad” scenes to life onstage and explore what surprisingly useful material might be hidden inside the chaos. Bring a scene from your own project or start from scratch.

Our only rule: no perfectionism allowed.

events.title: Lunch & Learn: Protecting Your Artistic Investment
events.blurb:
In this session, Max will walk you through securing rights, getting licenses, managing co-ownership issues among collaborators, and any other legal issue you can envision around your creative practice! Bring your questions!

Lunch will be provided.

events.title: Purple Noon (Plein Soleil)
events.blurb: Tom Ripley is a talented mimic, moocher, forger and all-around criminal improviser; but there's more to Tom Ripley than even he can guess.

events.title: The Louisiana Actor Experience, presented by SAGindie
events.blurb:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.

Louisiana-based union actors sit down for a raw and honest conversation about what it means to be an actor based here - the opportunities, the struggles, and what union membership really means for your career.

Sponsored by:

events.title: Filmmaking in Louisiana: A Town Hall Discussion
events.blurb:
OPEN TO NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!! NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED.

How can Louisiana filmmakers become better storytellers? What resources are at their disposal? In this town hall–style event, we bring together industry representatives from across Louisiana for an in-depth conversation about the current state of the independent film industry here.

events.title: Ripley's Game
events.blurb: Tom Ripley - cool, urbane, wealthy, and murderous - lives in a villa in the Veneto with Luisa, his harpsichord-playing girlfriend. A former business associate from Berlin's underworld pays a call asking Ripley's help in killing a rival. Ripley - ever a student of human nature - initiates a game to turn a mild and innocent local picture framer into a hit man. The artisan, Jonathan Trevanny, who's dying of cancer, has a wife, young son, and little to leave them. If Ripley draws Jonathan into the game, can Ripley maintain control? Does it stop at one killing? What if Ripley develops a conscience?

events.title: Louisiana Shorts: Encounters
events.blurb:
Featuring five World Premiers, these Louisiana short films showcase the most intriguing of human confrontations: from the magical to the mundane; the procedural to the personal; and the seemingly banal to the straight-up bizarre.

Shorts Block Sponsored by:

events.title: Pet Adoption Fair Before SCRIM Screening
events.blurb:
Bring the whole family to the Broadside for a special outdoor screening of the new film "Scrim: New Orleans' Most Famous Dog." And come early, from 6 to 7 PM for a pet adoption fair with local rescue organizations, where dogs and cats of all ages will be looking for their forever homes. You may leave with a new best friend of your own.

A NOFF Pass or Pay What You Will tickets to the Scrim screening required.

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
events.blurb: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.

events.title: The Oldest Person in the World
events.blurb: A decade-long global odyssey chronicles the ever-changing record holders of the title of oldest person alive. What begins as a portrait of longevity becomes a poignant meditation on the passage of time, the randomness of fate and the joy and profound human experience of being alive.

events.title: On the Last Day of Christmas
events.blurb: On Christmas Eve, a mother must protect her teenage son when their apartment building is overrun by demonic beings that begin hunting the residents.

events.title: Ephemera
events.blurb: On her last night in Shanghai, Chinese-American actress Asher asks out her hip-hop dance teacher Tori, sparking an electric, city-wide romance that must end by sunrise.

events.title: Last Night at the Palm Court
events.blurb: For 35 years, the Palm Court served traditional New Orleans jazz music and creole cuisine in the French Quarter. In May 2024, the restaurant closed its doors. This film tells the story of the staff, the players, and the music that made the club an international destination for fans of traditional jazz.

events.title: Dial Up Trivia: Soundtrack Attack
events.blurb:
FREE FOR NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!!

Honey Tangerine Productions presents Dial Up Trivia: Soundtrack Attack - a one-of-a-kind audio trivia night for film lovers! Think you can recognize a movie just by the score? Show us your skills at Dial Up Trivia: Soundtrack Attack! Prizes and bragging rights to the winners.

events.title: Independent Filmmaker Party
events.blurb:
FREE FOR NOFF ALL ACCESS PASSHOLDERS!!

Wrap up the weekend at the Broadside for a night that celebrates everything great about Louisiana and independent film. Under the open sky, mingle with filmmakers and friends over live music, local bites, and drinks aplenty. It's the kind of night that brings culture, community, and creativity together — a fitting close to the weekend.

events.title: Lunch & Learn: Louisiana Film Prize
events.blurb:
Join us for a Lunch & Learn focused on filmmaking in Louisiana and the opportunities available through the Louisiana Film Prize. We’ll explore how the Film Prize brings filmmakers and creative professionals together, supports local storytelling, and creates opportunities to connect with others working in the industry, all while offering the world’s largest cash prize for a narrative short film.

We'll focus on the importance of building and growing your filmmaking network—from finding collaborators and crew to connecting with other filmmakers, industry professionals, and local resources. Whether you’re an emerging filmmaker or an experienced creator, this will be an opportunity to learn more about Louisiana’s film community, discover ways to get involved, and make meaningful connections that can help move your next project forward.

Lunch will be provided.

Sponsored by:

events.blurb:
Introducing a curated selection of the next generation of New Orleans filmmaking talent! Totally unique in genre, subject matter and approach, these short films come from emerging directors out of Dillard, Loyola, Tulane, and the University of New Orleans (LSU).

events.title: Vindication to Victory
events.blurb: After a wrongful incarceration lands him behind bars for nearly 40 years, Raymond Flanks must adjust to life in the 21st century and chart his future in a world that's remarkably different from the one he remembers.
